question.text: Eight copper wire of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>l</mi></math> and diameter d are joined in parallel to form a single composite conductor of resistance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math>. If a single copper wire of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi>l</mi></math> have the same resistance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi>R</mi></mfenced></math> then its diameter will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi></math>.

solution.text:
Each wire has resistance, r=ρ4lπd2

Eight wire in parallel, then equivalent resistance is

R=r8=ρl2πd2

Single copper wire of length 2l has resistance R=ρ2l×4πd12.

Comparing both equations, we get,

ρ8lπd12=ρl2πd2

⇒d1=4d
